prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: rear-end collision in Conroe, Texas. Injury: concussion. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1175; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record, but my counsel has the information for the file.

Q: Understood. Where were you living at the time of the accident?
A: Here in the Conroe area, in Montgomery County, Texas.

Q: Let's talk about the collision. Where were you when it happened?
A: I was stopped at a traffic light on the main road, waiting for the light to change to green.

Q: What was the first thing you noticed?
A: I felt a hard jolt from behind. My head snapped forward and then back against the headrest. My car lurched into the intersection, and I remember my neck and the back of my head hitting something hard.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before impact?
A: No. I was looking at the light and checking my phone for directions. I didn't see it until the moment it hit me.

Q: Did you lose consciousness?
A: I don't think I fully blacked out, but I was dazed. I couldn't tell right away what had happened. A bystander came to my window and asked if I was okay, and I didn't have a clear answer.

Q: What symptoms did you have after the accident?
A: Headaches that wouldn't go away, ringing in my ears, and I felt nauseous most of the day. Bright lights bothered my eyes, and I had trouble concentrating on things I used to do without thinking.

Q: Did you seek medical treatment?
A: Yes. An ambulance took me to the emergency room that same day. They ran a CT scan and told me I had a concussion. They sent me home with instructions to rest in a dark room and avoid screens.

Q: Have you received any follow-up care?
A: I've seen my primary care doctor several times and was referred to a neurologist. I also started physical therapy for my neck, and I still go twice a week.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?
A: A lot. I used to work full days at my job, but I've had to cut back because I can't stay focused for long. I have to take breaks to lie down. I also stopped driving on highways because the motion and noise make my symptoms worse.

Q: What about your hobbies or family life?
A: I used to coach my nephew's soccer team and go hiking on weekends. I haven't been able to do either. My family has had to help more with errands and cooking, and I feel frustrated about that.

Q: Have you had any prior head injuries or neck problems?
A: No, nothing that required treatment. I had a minor fender bender years ago, but I didn't see a doctor for it and I didn't have lasting problems.
